findings.location: source.html | paragraph 3 (after figure) — bird species list
findings.source_quote: The robin opens up the choir in early spring, but his song is soon surpassed in beauty by the song sparrow and again by the rose-breasted grosbeak. The song of the wren trumps them all for longevity and vibrancy. The canary sings in a cage, while the nightingale sings in the dark. The robins sing in the rain. The buntings fill in the heat of the day when other birds are silent.
findings.suggested_fix: Either translate the English common names into Portuguese or consistently present them as English loanwords (and consider italicizing them). For example, replace 'robin' with 'tordo/robin (robin)', 'song sparrow' with 'song sparrow (song sparrow)' or 'pardal cantor', 'rose-breasted grosbeak' with 'grosbeak peitoral-rosado' or keep the English names consistently. Preserve the sentence structure and meaning while making bird names consistent in the target language.
findings.translation_quote: O robin abre o coro no início da primavera, mas seu canto logo é superado em beleza pelo song sparrow e novamente pelo rose‑breasted grosbeak. O canto do wren os ultrapassa a todos em longevidade e vivacidade. O canário canta numa gaiola, enquanto o nightingale canta no escuro. Os robins cantam na chuva. Os buntings preenchem o calor do dia quando outras aves estão silenciosas.

findings.source_quote: How little knowledge of heaven is committed to our understanding. The scenes of heavens described and laid out before us in Revelations can hardly bring our finite minds into its infinite realm.
findings.suggested_fix: The Portuguese rendering is slightly awkward/ambiguous: 'Quão pouco conhecimento do céu está comprometido à nossa compreensão.' Suggest a clearer phrasing that preserves the original sense, e.g. 'Quão pouco do conhecimento do céu foi confiado ao nosso entendimento' or 'Quão pouco conhecemos do céu'. Keep the following reference to 'Revelations' as in the source.
findings.translation_quote: Quão pouco conhecimento do céu está comprometido à nossa compreensão. As cenas dos céus descritas e postas diante de nós em Revelations dificilmente conseguem trazer nossas mentes finitas para seu reino infinito.

findings.location: source.html | paragraph 11 (Ingratitude section) — biblical/book names and capitalization consistency
findings.source_quote: “We hanged our harps upon the willows in the midst thereof. For there they that carried us away captive required of us a song; and they that wasted us required of us mirth, saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion. How shall we sing the LORD’S song in a strange land?” (Ps 137:2-4). God’s people had been instructed by Jeremiah to build houses, plant gardens and raise families. “… And seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried away captives..." (Jer. 29:5-7).
findings.suggested_fix: The translation preserves the original English biblical quotation (which is allowed), but consistency of book-name presentation in Portuguese text would improve clarity. Either keep all biblical book names in English as in the source (Jeremiah → 'Jeremiah') or translate them to Portuguese ('Jeremias'). Make this consistent across the article. Ensure the scripture citations (Ps, Jer., Col) match the presentation style chosen.
findings.translation_quote: “We hanged our harps upon the willows in the midst thereof. For there they that carried us away captive required of us a song; and they that wasted us required of us mirth, saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion. How shall we sing the LORD’S song in a strange land?” (Ps 137:2-4). O povo de Deus havia sido instruído por Jeremiah a construir casas, plantar jardins e criar famílias. “… And seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried away captives, and pray unto the LORD for it: for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace” (Jer. 29:5-7).
